date.as_written: saṃvat 967 sāla mi caitra śudi 1 roja 4

notes: The era is not named, but 'saṃvat 967 sāla' with a Newari colophon and a Newar Upādhyāya scribe points to Nepal Saṃvat, which gives about 1847 CE. 'brahmapūrachesa conā' means 'staying in the Brahmapūra house', and 'coyā sidhayakā julo' means 'finished writing'. A separate, corrupt Newari note follows, dated Phālguna vadi 11, ro 6 (Friday). It seems to say that Śakti gave this book in a dream ('śakti na svapne thva saphū vila') on the day of the Mīna-saṃkrānti. The phrase 'vipana sadhīrjavīraṃ yāṃ svapna' may hide a personal name, perhaps Dhīr(a)javīra, the person who had the dream. 'vāju' (father/elder) is also mentioned. The text is too uncertain to record either one as a person. The catalogue entry 'SAM 967' agrees with the colophon.
